tiarsdesigner.run_locus.get_enzyme_pair_stats_filtered(passed_enzymes_df, endogenous, locus, enzyme_pair_filters, codon_frequency_dict, verbose)[source]¶

given the candidates with enzymes that passed all four enzyme level filters, runs another set of filters on every possible pair of enzymes remaining for each candidate.

Parameters¶

passed_enzymes_df: pandas dataframe

A pandas dataframe that contains the passed candidate-enzyme combos. It should have a sequence column, a Renzyme column, a codon frequency column and an average distance to cas9 cutsite column.

endogenous: __init__.Endogenous object

An endogenous object that all of the remaining candidates are based on.

locus: string

The name of the locus; to be used in the csv file name if verbose == True

enzyme_pair_filters: list

A list of enzyme pair filters to use

codon_frequency_dict: dict

A dictionary with amino acid codons (e.g. ‘AGA’) as keys and the frequency with which they are used.

verbose: bool

A boolean value indicating whether or not to create a csv file from the output dataframe

Returns¶

A pandas dataframe with one row for each pair of passed enzymes for each candidate in passed_enzymes_df. The columns are ‘seq’ (sequence), Renzyme pair (a pair of Renzymes that each have at least one substitution dependent cutsite in its corresponding candidate sequence), result (boolean value indicating whether or not the Renzyme pair passed the filter for that row’s candidate), RenzymeA average distance to cas9 cut, RenzymeB average distance to cas9 cut, overall average distance to cas9 cut (average of previous 2), and codon frequency change. If the verbose option is selected, it will also create a csv called ‘[locus]_pair_filter_stats’ from the dataframe

tiarsdesigner.run_locus.get_docx_single(flat_passed_enzymes_df, no_unneeded_substitutions, endogenous, locus)[source]¶

Given a dataframe containing all of the candidate-enzyme combos that passed all of the filters, it further filters out any candidates with unneeded substitutions (if the filter is specified) and creates a docx file called ‘[locus]_single_Renzymes.docx to visualize all of the remaining candidate sequences and enzyme pairs. It will also create an xlsx file with more in-depth statistics on each candidate-Renzyme combo.

Parameters¶

flat_passed_enzymes_df: pandas dataframe

A pandas dataframe that contains the passed candidate-enzyme pair combos, with each combo getting its own row. It should have a sequence column, a Renzyme pair column, an average distance to cas9 cut column, a codon frequency change column, and a no unnneeded sustitutions column.

no_unneeded_substitutions: bool

Indicates whether the no_unneeded substitutions filter should be applied.

endogenous: __init__.Endogenous object

An endogenous object that all of the remaining candidates are based on.

locus: string

The name of the locus; to be used in the tsv file name if verbose == True

tiarsdesigner.run_locus.full_run(endogenous_seq, gRNA_start, gRNA_end, PAM_start, which_PAM, AA_change_site, new_codon, locus, single_enzyme_filters, enzyme_pair_filters, codon_usage_tsv, min_Rsite_distance=5, Renzymes=None, verbose=False)[source]¶

Given an endogenous sequence, desired edit + guideRNA, generates all the possible synonymous candidates for that sequence and runs all of the filters on them to get the final docx and xlsx files (one of each for both single enzymes and enzyme pairs) using the above functions. This is the only function for which the users will directly input the parameters (via commandline argparse).

Parameters¶

endogenous_seq: string

The endogenous/wt dna sequence without any synonymous changes and without the desired CRISPR facilitated amino acid change. Max length is 273 bp, must be in frame.

gRNA_start: int

the index location in the sequence of the beginning of the region the CRISPR/Cas9 guide RNA will target.

gRNA_end: int

the index location in the sequence of the end of the region the CRISPR/Cas9 guide RNA will target.

PAM_start: int

The index location in the sequence of the beginning of the PAM site. For now, the PAM region has to be either ‘CCN’ or ‘NGG’.

which_PAM: string

The sequence of the PAM site (e.g. ‘NGG’ or ‘CCN’ for cas9, or ‘TTTV’ or ‘BAAA’ for Cfp1)

AA_change_site: int

the index location in the sequence of the beginning of the codon that is to be nonsynonymously changed in the CRISPR/Cas9 process

new_codon: string

the codon to replace the existing codon at the AA_change_site

locus: string

The name of the locus; to be used in the csv file name if verbose == True

single_enzyme_filters: list

The number of single enzyme filters an enzyme needs to pass in order to stay in the running

enzyme_pair_filters: list

The number of paired enzyme filters a pair of enzymes needs to pass in order to stay in the running.

codon_usage_tsv: tsv

A tsv mapping codons to their usage frequency for the organism used

min_Rsite_distance (optional): int

The minimum allowable distance between the novel restriction site for an enzyme and any endogenous restriction sites it may have. This is to avoid having the fragment lengths after digestion be too similar to detect the difference between a novel site cut and an endogenous site cut. Default is 5 bp.

enzymes: (optional) string

A string indicating the path to a tsv file containing a list of enzymes to consider for the list of candidates. Default is the Bio.Restriction ‘AllEnzymes’ restriction batch.

verbose: (optional) bool

A boolean value indicating whether or not to create tsv files with filter statistics at each step. Default is False
